s.q: Magnitude and unit vector
s.f: |\vec a|=\sqrt{a_1^2+a_2^2+a_3^2},\qquad\hat a=\frac{\vec a}{|\vec a|}

s.q: Position vector of a dividing point
s.f: \vec r=\frac{m\vec b+n\vec a}{m+n}\ (\text{internal}),\qquad\frac{m\vec b-n\vec a}{m-n}\ (\text{external})

s.q: Direction cosines
s.f: l=\cos\alpha=\frac{a_1}{|\vec a|},\ \dots;\qquad l^2+m^2+n^2=1

s.q: Collinearity and coplanarity of points
s.f: \text{collinear}\iff\vec{AB}=\lambda\vec{AC};\qquad\text{coplanar}\iff[\vec{AB}\ \vec{AC}\ \vec{AD}]=0
s.n: Points $\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$ collinear iff there exist scalars, not all zero, with $x\vec a+y\vec b+z\vec c=\vec 0$ and $x+y+z=0$.

s.q: Vector between two points
s.f: \vec{AB}=\vec b-\vec a,\qquad|\vec{AB}|=\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2+(z_2-z_1)^2}

s.q: Types of vectors
s.f: \text{zero, unit, collinear (parallel), coplanar, equal, negative, co-initial, free}

s.q: Linear combination and independence
s.f: x\vec a+y\vec b+z\vec c=\vec0\ \text{only for } x=y=z=0\iff\text{non-coplanar}

s.q: Midpoint and centroid of a triangle
s.f: \frac{\vec a+\vec b}2,\qquad\frac{\vec a+\vec b+\vec c}3

s.q: Incentre in vectors
s.f: \frac{a\vec a+b\vec b+c\vec c}{a+b+c}

s.q: Angle a vector makes with axes
s.f: \cos\alpha=\frac{x}{|\vec r|},\ \cos\beta=\frac y{|\vec r|},\ \cos\gamma=\frac z{|\vec r|}

s.q: Scalar product
s.f: \vec a\cdot\vec b=|\vec a||\vec b|\cos\theta=a_1b_1+a_2b_2+a_3b_3
s.n: $\vec a\perp\vec b\iff\vec a\cdot\vec b=0$. $\hat i\cdot\hat i=1$, $\hat i\cdot\hat j=0$.

s.q: Projection
s.f: \text{projection of } \vec a \text{ on } \vec b=\frac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec b|};\qquad\text{vector projection}=\frac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec b|^2}\vec b

s.q: Work done
s.f: W=\vec F\cdot\vec d

s.q: Expansions
s.f: |\vec a\pm\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2+|\vec b|^2\pm2\vec a\cdot\vec b
s.n: $(\vec a+\vec b)\cdot(\vec a-\vec b)=|\vec a|^2-|\vec b|^2$; $|\vec a+\vec b|=|\vec a-\vec b|\iff\vec a\perp\vec b$.

s.q: Angle between two vectors
s.f: \cos\theta=\frac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec a||\vec b|}

s.q: Component of $\vec a$ along and perpendicular to $\vec b$
s.f: \vec a_\parallel=\frac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec b|^2}\vec b,\qquad\vec a_\perp=\vec a-\vec a_\parallel

s.q: Cauchy–Schwarz for vectors
s.f: |\vec a\cdot\vec b|\le|\vec a||\vec b|

s.q: Sum of squares of three vectors with equal magnitudes
s.f: |\vec a+\vec b+\vec c|^2=\sum|\vec a|^2+2\sum\vec a\cdot\vec b

s.q: Unit vectors with $|\hat a+\hat b|$ known
s.f: |\hat a+\hat b|=2\cos\frac\theta2,\qquad|\hat a-\hat b|=2\sin\frac\theta2

s.q: Vector product
s.f: \vec a\times\vec b=|\vec a||\vec b|\sin\theta\,\hat n=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\a_1&a_2&a_3\\b_1&b_2&b_3\end{vmatrix}
s.n: $\vec a\times\vec b=-\vec b\times\vec a$; parallel iff $\vec a\times\vec b=\vec0$. $\hat i\times\hat j=\hat k$, $\hat j\times\hat k=\hat i$, $\hat k\times\hat i=\hat j$.

s.q: Lagrange's identity
s.f: |\vec a\times\vec b|^2+(\vec a\cdot\vec b)^2=|\vec a|^2|\vec b|^2

s.q: Areas
s.f: \text{parallelogram}=|\vec a\times\vec b|,\quad\text{triangle}=\tfrac12|\vec a\times\vec b|,\quad\text{parallelogram (diagonals } \vec d_1,\vec d_2)=\tfrac12|\vec d_1\times\vec d_2|
s.n: Triangle with vertices $\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$: $\frac12|\vec a\times\vec b+\vec b\times\vec c+\vec c\times\vec a|$.

s.q: Moment (torque)
s.f: \vec M=\vec r\times\vec F

s.q: Unit vector perpendicular to both
s.f: \pm\frac{\vec a\times\vec b}{|\vec a\times\vec b|}

s.q: Sine of angle between vectors
s.f: \sin\theta=\frac{|\vec a\times\vec b|}{|\vec a||\vec b|}

s.q: Distributive and scalar properties
s.f: \vec a\times(\vec b+\vec c)=\vec a\times\vec b+\vec a\times\vec c,\qquad(k\vec a)\times\vec b=k(\vec a\times\vec b)

s.q: Area of quadrilateral with diagonals $\vec d_1,\vec d_2$
s.f: \frac12|\vec d_1\times\vec d_2|

s.q: Cross product of sum and difference
s.f: (\vec a+\vec b)\times(\vec a-\vec b)=-2\,\vec a\times\vec b

s.q: Distance of a point from a line in vector form
s.f: \frac{|(\vec p-\vec a)\times\vec b|}{|\vec b|}

s.q: Scalar triple product
s.f: [\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]=\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)=\begin{vmatrix}a_1&a_2&a_3\\b_1&b_2&b_3\\c_1&c_2&c_3\end{vmatrix}
s.n: Volume of parallelepiped; tetrahedron $=\frac16|[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]|$. Cyclic shifts keep the value; swapping two changes sign; zero iff coplanar.

s.q: Products of triple products
s.f: [\vec a\times\vec b\ \ \vec b\times\vec c\ \ \vec c\times\vec a]=[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]^2
s.n: $[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c][\vec p\ \vec q\ \vec r]=\begin{vmatrix}\vec a\cdot\vec p&\vec a\cdot\vec q&\vec a\cdot\vec r\\\vec b\cdot\vec p&\cdots\\\vec c\cdot\vec p&\cdots\end{vmatrix}$.

s.q: Vector triple product
s.f: \vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)=(\vec a\cdot\vec c)\vec b-(\vec a\cdot\vec b)\vec c
s.n: $(\vec a\times\vec b)\times\vec c=(\vec a\cdot\vec c)\vec b-(\vec b\cdot\vec c)\vec a$ — not associative.

s.q: Product of two cross products
s.f: (\vec a\times\vec b)\cdot(\vec c\times\vec d)=\begin{vmatrix}\vec a\cdot\vec c&\vec a\cdot\vec d\\\vec b\cdot\vec c&\vec b\cdot\vec d\end{vmatrix}
s.n: $(\vec a\times\vec b)\times(\vec c\times\vec d)=[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec d]\vec c-[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]\vec d$.

s.q: Reciprocal system
s.f: \vec a'=\frac{\vec b\times\vec c}{[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]},\ \text{etc.};\quad\vec a\cdot\vec a'=1,\ \ [\vec a'\ \vec b'\ \vec c'][\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]=1

s.q: Scalar triple product with repeated vector
s.f: [\vec a\ \vec a\ \vec b]=0

s.q: Linear property of STP
s.f: [\vec a+\vec b\ \ \vec c\ \ \vec d]=[\vec a\ \vec c\ \vec d]+[\vec b\ \vec c\ \vec d]

s.q: STP of sums
s.f: [\vec a+\vec b\ \ \vec b+\vec c\ \ \vec c+\vec a]=2[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c],\qquad[\vec a-\vec b\ \ \vec b-\vec c\ \ \vec c-\vec a]=0

s.q: Volume of tetrahedron with vertices $\vec a,\vec b,\vec c,\vec d$
s.f: \frac16\left|[\vec b-\vec a\ \ \vec c-\vec a\ \ \vec d-\vec a]\right|

s.q: STP of unit vectors along the axes
s.f: [\hat i\ \hat j\ \hat k]=1

s.q: Vector triple product sum identity (Jacobi)
s.f: \vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)+\vec b\times(\vec c\times\vec a)+\vec c\times(\vec a\times\vec b)=\vec0

s.q: $\hat i\times(\vec a\times\hat i)+\cdots$
s.f: \hat i\times(\vec a\times\hat i)+\hat j\times(\vec a\times\hat j)+\hat k\times(\vec a\times\hat k)=2\vec a

s.q: Sum of squares of cross products with axes
s.f: |\vec a\times\hat i|^2+|\vec a\times\hat j|^2+|\vec a\times\hat k|^2=2|\vec a|^2

s.q: Any vector in terms of three non-coplanar vectors
s.f: \vec r=\frac{[\vec r\ \vec b\ \vec c]\vec a+[\vec a\ \vec r\ \vec c]\vec b+[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec r]\vec c}{[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]}

s.q: Angle bisector direction
s.f: \hat a+\hat b\ (\text{internal}),\qquad\hat a-\hat b\ (\text{external})

s.q: Solving $\vec r\times\vec b=\vec a\times\vec b$ and $\vec r\cdot\vec c=0$
s.f: \vec r=\vec a-\frac{\vec a\cdot\vec c}{\vec b\cdot\vec c}\vec b
s.n: First equation gives $\vec r=\vec a+\lambda\vec b$; fix $\lambda$ from the second.

s.q: Solving $\vec x+\vec x\times\vec a=\vec b$
s.f: \vec x=\frac{\vec b+(\vec a\cdot\vec b)\vec a+\vec a\times\vec b}{1+|\vec a|^2}
s.d: Take dot and cross with $\vec a$ to find $\vec x\cdot\vec a$ and $\vec x\times\vec a$, then substitute.

s.q: Medians, centroid, and vector proofs
s.f: \text{centroid}=\frac{\vec a+\vec b+\vec c}3,\qquad\text{tetrahedron centroid}=\frac{\vec a+\vec b+\vec c+\vec d}4

s.q: Vector perpendicular to $\vec a$ in the plane of $\vec a$, $\vec b$
s.f: \vec a\times(\vec a\times\vec b)\ \ \text{or}\ \ \vec b-\frac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec a|^2}\vec a

s.q: Vector of given magnitude along the bisector
s.f: \lambda\left(\hat a+\hat b\right)

s.q: Coplanarity of four points
s.f: [\vec b-\vec a\ \ \vec c-\vec a\ \ \vec d-\vec a]=0

s.q: Solving $\vec r\cdot\vec a=p$, $\vec r\times\vec b=\vec c$
s.f: \vec r=\frac{p\,\vec b+\vec a\times\vec c}{\vec a\cdot\vec b}\quad(\text{needs } \vec a\cdot\vec b\ne0,\ \vec b\cdot\vec c=0)
s.d: Cross $\vec a$ with $\vec r\times\vec b=\vec c$: $\vec a\times(\vec r\times\vec b)=(\vec a\cdot\vec b)\vec r-(\vec a\cdot\vec r)\vec b=\vec a\times\vec c$; put $\vec a\cdot\vec r=p$.

s.q: Angle between diagonals of a cube / faces
s.f: \cos^{-1}\frac13\ (\text{body diagonals});\qquad\text{face diagonals on adjacent faces}: 60^\circ

s.q: Maximum of $\vec a\cdot\vec b$ and $|\vec a\times\vec b|$
s.f: |\vec a||\vec b|\ \text{each (at } \theta=0 \text{ and } \tfrac\pi2)

s: If this type comes, solve like this

s.q: If $\vec c$ satisfies a cross-product equation like $\vec c\times\vec b=\vec a\times\vec b$ plus a dot condition
s.r: "$\vec c\times\vec b=\vec a\times\vec b$ and $\vec c\cdot\vec a=0$", "$(\vec a+\vec b+\vec c)\times\vec c=\vec0$", "$\vec c\times\vec u=\vec u\times\vec d$", "$(\vec a+\vec b)\times\vec c=2(\vec a\times\vec b)+\ldots$".
s.f: \vec p\times\vec b=\vec0\ (\vec b\ne\vec0)\iff\vec p=\lambda\vec b
s.s: Move everything to one side and factor: $(\vec c-\vec a)\times\vec b=\vec0$. || Conclude $\vec c=\vec a+\lambda\vec b$ (one unknown scalar instead of three components). || Use the dot condition to find $\lambda$. || If the equation has no common factor, write $\vec c=(x,y,z)$, expand and compare components.
s.e: $\vec c\times\vec b=\vec a\times\vec b$, $\vec c\cdot\vec a=0$ ⇒ $\vec c=\vec a+\lambda\vec b$ with $|\vec a|^2+\lambda\,\vec a\cdot\vec b=0$.

s.q: If $\vec x$ lies in the plane of $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ and satisfies dot/magnitude conditions
s.r: "$\vec x$ in the plane of $\vec a,\vec b$ and perpendicular to $\vec u$", "$\vec c$ coplanar with $\vec a,\vec b$, $\vec a\cdot\vec c=7$, $\vec b\perp\vec c$", "$\vec d$ of magnitude 2 in the yz-plane".
s.f: \vec x=\lambda\vec a+\mu\vec b\quad\text{or}\quad\vec x=t\,\vec u\times(\vec a\times\vec b)
s.s: Write $\vec x=\lambda\vec a+\mu\vec b$. || Each dot condition gives one linear equation in $\lambda,\mu$. || A magnitude condition fixes the remaining scale. || If $\vec x\perp\vec u$ and in the plane of $\vec a,\vec b$, then $\vec x\parallel\vec u\times(\vec a\times\vec b)$.

s.q: If $\vec a\times\vec b=\vec c$ and $\vec b\times\vec c=\vec a$ type cyclic relations or collinearity conditions are given
s.r: "$\vec a\times\vec b=\vec c$, $\vec b\times\vec c=\vec a$, $|\vec a|=2$", "$\vec a+5\vec b\parallel\vec c$ and $\vec b+6\vec c\parallel\vec a$", "$\vec a\times\vec b=\vec c$ and $\vec a\cdot\vec b=1$".
s.f: \vec a\times\vec b=\vec c\Rightarrow\vec c\perp\vec a,\ \vec c\perp\vec b;\quad\vec b=\frac{\vec c\times\vec a+(\vec a\cdot\vec b)\vec a}{|\vec a|^2}
s.s: From cross relations, the vectors are mutually perpendicular; take magnitudes to get $|\vec a|\,|\vec b|=|\vec c|$ etc. || For "$\vec a\times\vec b=\vec c$, $\vec a\cdot\vec b=k$", solve $\vec b$ with the formula (cross both sides with $\vec a$). || For collinearity, write $\vec a+5\vec b=\lambda\vec c$, $\vec b+6\vec c=\mu\vec a$ and compare coefficients of the independent vectors $\vec b,\vec c$.

s.q: If magnitudes and dot products are given and $|\vec a\pm\vec b|$, an angle, or a max value is asked
s.r: "$|\vec a|=1$, $|\vec b|=4$, $\vec a\cdot\vec b=2$; angle between $\vec b$ and $2\vec a\times\vec b-3\vec b$", "$(\vec a+3\vec b)\perp(7\vec a-5\vec b)$…", "max of $3|3\vec a+2\vec b|+4|3\vec a-2\vec b|$".
s.f: |\vec a\pm\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2+|\vec b|^2\pm2\vec a\cdot\vec b,\quad|\vec a\times\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2|\vec b|^2-(\vec a\cdot\vec b)^2
s.s: Square the magnitude you need and expand with dot products. || $\vec a\times\vec b$ is perpendicular to both, so its dot with them is 0. || Perpendicularity gives equations in $|\vec a|^2,|\vec b|^2,\vec a\cdot\vec b$; solve them. || For max of $p|\vec u|+q|\vec v|$ with $|\vec u|^2+|\vec v|^2$ fixed, use Cauchy–Schwarz.

s.q: If the sides of a triangle are vectors with given lengths and a projection or dot product is asked
s.r: "$|BC|=8$, $|CA|=7$, $|AB|=10$; projection of $\vec{AB}$ on $\vec{AC}$", "$\vec a+\vec b+\vec c=\vec0$ with given magnitudes".
s.f: \vec a+\vec b+\vec c=\vec0\Rightarrow\vec a\cdot\vec b=\frac{|\vec c|^2-|\vec a|^2-|\vec b|^2}2
s.s: Write the closing relation $\vec{BC}+\vec{CA}+\vec{AB}=\vec0$. || Square a rearranged version to get each dot product. || Projection of $\vec{AB}$ on $\vec{AC}$ $=\frac{\vec{AB}\cdot\vec{AC}}{|AC|}$ (cosine rule in vector form).

s.q: If three vectors are mutually perpendicular with equal magnitudes, or coplanar at equal angles
s.r: "$\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$ mutually perpendicular, same magnitude, and $\vec a\times\{(\vec r-\vec b)\times\vec a\}+\ldots=\vec0$", "coplanar concurrent vectors at equal angles ($120^\circ$)", "$(x\vec a+y\vec b)\perp(6y\vec a-18x\vec b)$ for all $x,y$".
s.f: \vec a\times(\vec p\times\vec a)=|\vec a|^2\vec p-(\vec a\cdot\vec p)\vec a
s.s: Expand the triple cross products with the BAC–CAB rule. || Use $\vec a\cdot\vec b=0$ etc. and equal magnitudes $k$. || Collect terms to solve for $\vec r$ (often $\vec r=\frac{\vec a+\vec b+\vec c}2$). || "For all $x,y$" means each coefficient of $x^2$, $xy$, $y^2$ must vanish.

s.q: If the projection of one vector on another is asked
s.r: "Projection of $\vec b-2\vec a$ on $\vec a\times\ldots$", "$\vec c$ = projection vector of $\vec b$ on $\vec a$ and $|\vec a+\vec c|=7$", "vector making equal angles with the axes with given projection".
s.f: \text{scalar projection of }\vec b\text{ on }\vec a=\frac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec a|},\quad\text{projection vector}=\frac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec a|^2}\vec a
s.s: Find the unknown components from the given conditions first (e.g. compare $\vec a\times\vec b$ componentwise). || Apply the projection formula. || "Equal angles with the axes" means components are equal: $\vec a=k(1,1,1)$.

s.q: If a vector must make given angles with other vectors, or an angle must be obtuse for all $t$
s.r: "Unit vector at $60^\circ$ with $2\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k$ and $45^\circ$ with $\hat i-\hat k$", "$\hat a\perp\vec b,\vec c$ and at angle $\cos^{-1}(-\frac13)$ with…", "obtuse for all $t\in\mathbb R$".
s.f: \vec u\cdot\vec v=|\vec u||\vec v|\cos\theta;\ \ \text{obtuse for all } t\iff\vec a\cdot\vec b<0\ \forall t
s.s: Write the unknown unit vector $(x,y,z)$ with $x^2+y^2+z^2=1$. || Each angle condition is a linear equation in $x,y,z$. || Solve the two linear equations and the unit condition. || For "obtuse for all $t$", $\vec a\cdot\vec b$ is a quadratic in $t$: need leading coefficient $<0$ and $D<0$.

s.q: If a 2D vector is rotated about the origin
s.r: "$\vec v_2=2\hat i+(p+1)\hat j$ is obtained by rotating $\vec v_1=\sqrt3p\hat i+\hat j$ by $\theta$", "rotate $\sqrt3\hat i+\hat j$ by $45^\circ$".
s.f: |\vec v_1|=|\vec v_2|;\ \ (x,y)\to(x\cos\theta-y\sin\theta,\ x\sin\theta+y\cos\theta)
s.s: Rotation keeps the length: equate magnitudes to find the parameter. || The angle from $\cos\theta=\frac{\vec v_1\cdot\vec v_2}{|\vec v_1|^2}$, or apply the rotation formula directly.

s.q: If coplanarity is tested (scalar triple product zero) for vectors or points
s.r: "$\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$ coplanar; find $\lambda$", "four points $(1,5,35)$, $(7,5,5)$, … coplanar", "$\vec c$ coplanar with $\vec a,\vec b$, $\vec a\cdot\vec c=5$, $\vec b\perp\vec c$".
s.f: [\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]=\begin{vmatrix}a_1&a_2&a_3\\b_1&b_2&b_3\\c_1&c_2&c_3\end{vmatrix}=0
s.s: For vectors, set the determinant of components to zero. || For four points $A,B,C,D$, use $[\vec{AB}\ \vec{AC}\ \vec{AD}]=0$. || Solve for the parameter; discard values making two vectors equal/parallel if the question needs "non-collinear".

s.q: If a volume (parallelepiped or tetrahedron) is asked
s.r: "Volume $V$ with edges $\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$; volume with edges $\vec a+\vec b$, $\vec b+\vec c$, …", "local max of $\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)$", "altitude of a tetrahedron", "edges $AB,AC,AD$ mutually perpendicular with face areas 5, 6, 7".
s.f: V_{\text{par}}=|[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]|,\ \ V_{\text{tet}}=\tfrac16|[\vec{AB}\ \vec{AC}\ \vec{AD}]|,\ \ [\vec a+\vec b\ \ \vec b+\vec c\ \ \vec c+\vec a]=2[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]
s.s: Express the new edges as combinations of $\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$; the new triple product is the determinant of the coefficient matrix times $[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]$. || Altitude from $D$ = $\frac{3V}{\text{area of }ABC}$. || For a right-corner tetrahedron, the far face area satisfies $\Delta^2=\Delta_1^2+\Delta_2^2+\Delta_3^2$.
s.e: Face areas 5, 6, 7 at a right corner: far face $=\sqrt{25+36+49}=\sqrt{110}$.

s.q: If the area of a triangle/parallelogram is found with position vectors
s.r: "$\vec{AB}$, $\vec{CB}$, $\vec{CA}$ given with unknown components and area given", "sides of a triangle given as vectors", "area of the parallelogram on $\vec a$ and $\vec c$".
s.f: \text{area of }\triangle=\tfrac12|\vec{AB}\times\vec{AC}|,\quad\text{parallelogram}=|\vec a\times\vec b|,\ \ \text{on diagonals}=\tfrac12|\vec d_1\times\vec d_2|
s.s: Use $\vec{AB}=\vec{AC}+\vec{CB}$ to find unknown components. || Compute the cross product and its magnitude. || Use the area condition to solve for the parameter.

s.q: If a point divides a segment, lies on an angle bisector, or is a centroid (position vectors)
s.r: "$P$ divides $AB$ in $\lambda:1$", "internal bisector of $\angle AOB$ meets $AB$ at $C$", "centroid $G$ of $ABC$; $\cos\angle GOA$", "$E,F$ mid-points of the diagonals".
s.f: \text{internal division: }\frac{m\vec b+n\vec a}{m+n};\ \ \text{bisector from O divides } AB \text{ in } OA:OB
s.s: Write the point with the section formula. || For a bisector, the ratio is the ratio of the adjacent side lengths. || Centroid $=\frac{\vec a+\vec b+\vec c}3$. || Then compute the asked angle/length with dot products.

s.q: Mixed vector facts (rhombus diagonals, $\tan\theta_k$ vectors, inequalities between components, point equidistant from three points)
s.r: Rhombus with given opposite vertices, $\sum|\vec a_k|^2$, "$\max|a_i|\le|\vec a|\le3\max|a_i|$", statements to check.
s.f: \text{rhombus: diagonals bisect each other at right angles}
s.s: Translate geometry into vector conditions (perpendicular → dot zero; midpoint; equal distances). || Compute with components. || For statement questions, test each claim separately with a quick calculation or counterexample.
